about: Quirks: strengths the grader can award, 4 per pillar. Mistakes (error_codes.json) are shown to people as antiquirks. Ids are internal; people see plain_name, earned_line and how_to_earn. `opposes` lists the antiquirk codes that cancel the quirk on the same question.

quirks.earned_line: You used a maths rule correctly in a spot where it is easy to slip.
quirks.how_to_earn: Use a rule like the power laws or the distributive property correctly where it matters.
quirks.description: The student correctly applied a key rule that the question hinges on (exponent laws, distributing over a bracket, combining like terms, a trig ratio, the zero-product property) at a point where students commonly slip.

quirks.earned_line: Every time you changed one side of the equation, you changed the other side the same way.
quirks.how_to_earn: Solve an equation in several steps, doing the same thing to both sides every time.
quirks.description: Across a multi-step equation solution (at least two rearranging steps), every operation was applied to both sides of the equation.

quirks.earned_line: You wrote down why a step works, not just what you did.
quirks.how_to_earn: Add a short reason beside a step, like "opposite angles are equal" or "the slopes are equal so the lines are parallel".
quirks.description: The student wrote a correct reason, property or justification in words or symbols (e.g. naming the theorem, the angle property, why lines are parallel), showing understanding beyond the procedure.

quirks.earned_line: You noticed a value that is not allowed and dealt with it.
quirks.how_to_earn: Reject an answer that does not make sense, like a negative length, or note a value the variable cannot be.
quirks.description: The student explicitly noticed and handled a restriction: rejected an extraneous or impossible root (negative length, negative time), stated a domain restriction, or noted a value that makes a denominator zero.

quirks.earned_line: You turned the question into the right equation and said what your letters stand for.
quirks.how_to_earn: Start a word problem with "Let x be ..." and write the right equation from the words.
quirks.description: The student set the problem up correctly from words or context and made the setup readable: defined variables ("let x be ...") or clearly listed the givens, and the first equation or formula is correct.

quirks.earned_line: You picked a method that made the question quicker and cleaner.
quirks.how_to_earn: Choose the method that fits, like elimination when the numbers line up, or factoring when the quadratic factors nicely.
quirks.description: The student chose a notably efficient and suitable method for this question (e.g. elimination when coefficients already match, factoring instead of the formula when it factors, a shortcut property) and it worked. Do not award it for the only reasonable method.

quirks.earned_line: You drew or labelled a diagram to plan your answer.
quirks.how_to_earn: Sketch the triangle, graph or situation and label what you know before you start.
quirks.description: The student drew, or correctly labelled, a diagram or sketch of their own (triangle with sides marked, a quick graph, a number line) that supports the solution. The transcription or affect markers must show it.

quirks.earned_line: You found every answer, not just the first one.
quirks.how_to_earn: When there can be more than one answer, like the two roots of a quadratic or a plus-or-minus square root, find them all.
quirks.description: The question has more than one case or solution (two roots, plus-or-minus square root, two possible triangles, both intersection points) and the student found all of them.

quirks.earned_line: Each line of your work follows clearly from the one before.
quirks.how_to_earn: Write one change per line so anyone can follow how you got from the question to the answer.
quirks.description: Every key step in the answer key is PRESENT or EQUIVALENT_METHOD in key_step_checks, with no jumps, and the work is long enough (at least three lines) for this to matter.

quirks.earned_line: You kept every negative sign and term through a long rearrangement.
quirks.how_to_earn: Rearrange an equation with negatives in it without losing a sign or a term.
quirks.description: The student rearranged or expanded an expression containing negative terms over several lines without dropping a sign, term or factor.

quirks.earned_line: You factored correctly the first time.
quirks.how_to_earn: Factor a trinomial, a difference of squares or a common factor correctly.
quirks.description: The student factored an expression correctly (common factor, trinomial, difference of squares, grouping) where factoring was part of the method.

quirks.earned_line: You simplified your answer all the way down.
quirks.how_to_earn: Finish by collecting like terms and reducing fractions and roots as far as they go.
quirks.description: The final answer is in fully simplified form where simplifying took real work (reduced fraction, simplified radical, collected like terms, combined systems cleanly).

quirks.earned_line: All your calculations were right, even the long ones.
quirks.how_to_earn: Get through a question with several calculations and no arithmetic slips.
quirks.description: The question involved substantial arithmetic (several multiplications, divisions or multi-digit operations) and every calculation was correct.

quirks.earned_line: You worked with negative numbers without a slip.
quirks.how_to_earn: Multiply, divide or subtract negative numbers correctly.
quirks.description: The student computed correctly with negative numbers in places where sign slips are common (subtracting a negative, squaring a negative, multiplying two negatives).

quirks.earned_line: You kept full accuracy until the end and rounded the way the question asked.
quirks.how_to_earn: Keep the full number on your calculator until the last step, then round as the question says.
quirks.description: The answer required rounding or a decimal approximation and the student kept accuracy through the work and rounded correctly at the end.

quirks.earned_line: You wrote a formula from memory and got it exactly right.
quirks.how_to_earn: Write a formula like the quadratic formula, distance formula or a trig ratio correctly from memory.
quirks.description: The student wrote out a formula that the question did not give (quadratic formula, distance or midpoint formula, slope, Pythagorean theorem, a trig ratio, sine or cosine law) and it is exactly right.

quirks.earned_line: Your final answer has the right units.
quirks.how_to_earn: Put units like cm, m² or degrees on answers that need them.
quirks.description: The answer needed units (lengths, areas, angles, money, time) and the student wrote the correct units on the final answer.

quirks.earned_line: You finished with a sentence that answers the question.
quirks.how_to_earn: End a word problem with a sentence like "The ladder reaches 4.2 m up the wall."
quirks.description: The question was a word or context problem and the student ended with a clear concluding statement that answers what was asked, in context.

quirks.earned_line: Your work is neat and easy to follow from top to bottom.
quirks.how_to_earn: Write one step per line, lined up, with your final answer clearly marked.
quirks.description: The work is laid out in a clean, ordered way (one step per line, equals signs lined up, final answer boxed or underlined) and the affect markers show clean, continuous flow rather than cramped or scratched-out writing.

quirks.earned_line: You used equals signs, brackets and symbols the right way.
quirks.how_to_earn: Use an equals sign only between things that are equal, and keep brackets where they belong.
quirks.description: The student used notation correctly throughout a non-trivial solution: no run-on equals signs, brackets kept where needed, correct symbols for angles, roots, plus-or-minus and labels.

quirks.earned_line: You checked your answer by putting it back into the question.
quirks.how_to_earn: When you finish, substitute your answer back in to see if it works.
quirks.description: The student's own work shows a check: substituting the answer back into the original equation(s), checking against an estimate, or verifying a constraint. It must be written on the page.

quirks.earned_line: You answered every part of the question.
quirks.how_to_earn: Answer every part, (a), (b) and (c), even if you are not sure of one.
quirks.description: The question has two or more parts or asks for two or more things, and the student attempted every one.

quirks.earned_line: You kept working through a hard question instead of giving up.
quirks.how_to_earn: Stick with a tough question and reach an answer, even if you get stuck along the way.
quirks.description: The affect markers or the work show the student hit difficulty (scratch-outs, a question mark, a restart) but persisted and reached a final answer.

quirks.earned_line: You spotted a mistake in your own work and fixed it.
quirks.how_to_earn: Look back over your work, find something that is wrong and correct it.
quirks.description: The page shows the student crossed out or corrected a wrong line and replaced it with a correct one. Do not award it if the crossed-out work was actually right.
